cells.Values and default: Integer count of requests. The script uses the text in bash arithmetic. The script does not validate it. Unset: 8 requests.
cells.Effect: `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to the URL in `API_URL`) sends this number of requests. Each request starts at a random time inside the arrival window that `WINDOW_MS` sets. The option `-n` or `--num-users` overrides the variable.

cells.Values and default: `random` or `cycle`, as exact text. Any other text stops the script with exit status 1. Unset: `random`.
cells.Effect: `random` draws the system prompt and the user question at random for each request of `burst-test.sh`. `cycle` takes the 256 pairs of 16 system prompts and 16 user questions in a fixed order. The option `-c` or `--cycle-prompts` sets `cycle` and overrides the variable. The script sends the user question only when `PROMPT_MODE` is `short`.

cells.Values and default: `long` or `short`, as exact text. Any other text stops the script with exit status 1. Unset: `long`.
cells.Effect: `long` makes `burst-test.sh` send an English passage and ask the model to repeat it. The passage size is drawn at random between `PROMPT_TOKENS_MIN` and `PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX`. `short` sends one of 16 short questions. The option `-s` or `--short-prompts` sets `short` and overrides the variable.

cells.Values and default: Integer number of estimated tokens. It must not be smaller than `PROMPT_TOKENS_MIN`. Otherwise the script exits with status 1. Unset: 15000 estimated tokens.
cells.Effect: It is the upper limit of the prompt size when `PROMPT_MODE` is `long`. Each request of `burst-test.sh` draws its size at random between `PROMPT_TOKENS_MIN` and `PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX`. The script header says that the context window of the model must cover `PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX` plus `MAX_TOKENS_BASE` plus `MAX_TOKENS_JITTER`. The script counts 3 words as 4 tokens. It builds the passage from whole paragraphs. The passage can be larger than the drawn size. The range check also runs when `PROMPT_MODE` is `short`. The option `-P` or `--prompt-max` overrides the variable.

cells.Values and default: Integer number of estimated tokens. It must be at least 1 and not larger than `PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX`. Otherwise the script exits with status 1. Unset: 1000 estimated tokens.
cells.Effect: It is the lower limit of the prompt size when `PROMPT_MODE` is `long`. Each request of `burst-test.sh` draws its size at random between `PROMPT_TOKENS_MIN` and `PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX`. The script counts 3 words as 4 tokens. The range check also runs when `PROMPT_MODE` is `short`. The option `-p` or `--prompt-min` overrides the variable.

cells.Values and default: Integer. The script assigns the text to the bash variable `RANDOM`. The script does not check the text. Unset: the script does not seed `RANDOM`.
cells.Effect: `burst-test.sh` assigns a non-empty value to the bash variable `RANDOM` before the first random draw. The draws of arrival offsets, `max_tokens` values, prompt sizes and prompt pairs then come from the seeded generator. The script comment says that a fixed value reproduces the schedule. The option `-S` or `--seed` overrides the variable. `long` mode makes 3 more draws for each request than `short` mode. The same value then gives a different schedule in `long` mode and in `short` mode.

cells.Values and default: `true` or `false`. The script compares the text with `true`. It also passes the text to `jq` as the JSON value of the request field `stream`. Unset: `true`.
cells.Effect: `true` makes `burst-test.sh` send streaming requests. The script then checks that each stream ends with `[DONE]` and holds no error frame. `false` sends blocking requests. The option `-b` or `--blocking` sets `false` and overrides the variable. Text that is not JSON, for example `yes`, makes `jq` fail. That request is not sent and counts as failed. Other JSON, for example `1`, is sent as written and handled as blocking.

cells.Values and default: `perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh`: only the exact text `true` turns it on. `rust/rust-toolchain.sh`: any non-empty text turns it on. Unset: off in both scripts.
cells.Effect: Two unrelated scripts read it. `perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh` (the request generator for Perfetto captures) prints the text of each model response. `rust/rust-toolchain.sh` (the Rust version check and setup script) prints its information messages. In `burst-test.sh`, the option `-v` or `--verbose` sets it to `true`. CMake runs `rust/rust-toolchain.sh` at configure time and prints its output. An exported value adds the messages there. The option `-v` of `rust-toolchain.sh` also turns on shell tracing. The variable alone does not.

cells.Values and default: Whole number of milliseconds. The script uses the text in bash arithmetic and does not validate it. Unset: 5000 milliseconds (5 seconds).
cells.Effect: Sets the arrival window of `perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh` (the request generator for Perfetto captures). Each request starts at a random offset from 0 milliseconds to less than this value. The option `-w` or `--window-ms` overrides it. With `0`, every request starts at offset 0 milliseconds.

cells.Set by: The Nix apps `tronperf` and `wrapper`, two CI workflows, or a developer.
cells.Values and default: Path of a directory. `tronperf` and `wrapper` need executable files `perfetto`, `traced` and `traced_probes` in it. `perfetto_capture.py` needs the files `traced` and `perfetto`. Unset: `perfetto/tronperf` and `perfetto/wrapper` use `$PERFETTO_HOME/out/linux`. `nix run .#tronperf` and `nix run .#wrapper` use the Nix package `perfetto-host-binaries`. `resolve-perfetto-bin-dir.sh` builds that package. `perfetto_capture.py` raises `RuntimeError`.
cells.Effect: `tronperf` and `wrapper` (the Perfetto capture scripts in `perfetto/`) start `perfetto`, `traced` and `traced_probes` from this directory. `bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py` starts `traced` and `perfetto` from it. `bin/ci/resolve-perfetto-bin-dir.sh` prints a non-empty value unchanged and runs no build. It takes priority over `PERFETTO_HOME`. In `perfetto_capture.py` the option `--bin-dir` takes priority over it. A missing program stops `tronperf` and `wrapper` with exit status 2. `bin/ci/test-perfetto-capture.sh` runs its integration checks only when the directory holds executable `traced` and `perfetto`.

cells.Set by: A developer who uses a custom Perfetto build.
cells.Values and default: Path of a directory. The scripts use its sub-directory `out/linux`. That sub-directory must hold executable files `perfetto`, `traced` and `traced_probes`. Unset: no effect. When `PERFETTO_BIN_DIR` is also unset or empty, `tronperf` and `wrapper` print an error and exit with status 2.
cells.Effect: `tronperf` and `wrapper` (the Perfetto capture scripts in `perfetto/`) start `perfetto`, `traced` and `traced_probes` from `$PERFETTO_HOME/out/linux`. The scripts use `PERFETTO_HOME` only when `PERFETTO_BIN_DIR` is unset or empty. `nix run .#tronperf` and `nix run .#wrapper` always export a non-empty `PERFETTO_BIN_DIR`. `PERFETTO_HOME` then has no effect. A missing program stops the script with exit status 2. `bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py` does not read `PERFETTO_HOME`.

cells.Set by: A developer who wants the trace on another host.
cells.Values and default: Host name or address of an `scp` destination. `tronperf` adds `:` after the text. `tronperf` does not check the text. Unset: `tronperf` does not copy the trace.
cells.Effect: After a capture without errors, `tronperf` (the script that captures a Perfetto trace of one runtron run) copies the trace file to that host with `scp -C`. The destination has no path. `scp` then writes the file into the home directory of the remote user. `tronperf` skips the copy when runtron, the `perfetto` client or a Perfetto daemon ends with an error. When `scp` fails, `tronperf` exits with the `scp` status. The trace file is `$HOME/runtron.trace`, or the path given with `--output-file`. `perfetto/wrapper` does not read the variable.
